Mitochondria are membrane-bound organelles found in most eukaryotic cells. The Mitochondria generate most of the cell's supply of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), used as a source of chemical energy.

Photosynthesis is the process used by plants to convert light energy into chemical energy. During Photosynthesis, chlorophyll in the chloroplast absorbs sunlight.

Unlike chloroplasts, Mitochondria are found in both plant and animal cells. The Mitochondria has its own DNA, separate from the cell's nuclear DNA.

Photosynthesis occurs mainly in the leaves of plants, within structures called chloroplasts. The products of Photosynthesis include glucose and oxygen.

Cells rely on the Mitochondria for energy production, which is why it's often called the powerhouse of the cell.
